builder_plan.scenario: A narrow, repeated product task may not need your largest model.
builder_plan.change: Check whether a released student model fits the task before generating training data.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current model and an off-the-shelf small model on the same held-out tasks.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Student quality, serving cost, teacher calls, training cost, and failures on unusual inputs.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: AutoMaster: Autonomous Post-Training by Making the Same Model a Better Teacher
summary: AutoMaster replaces Vanilla SFT on raw successful teacher trajectories with SFT on skill-guided trajectories, where an LLM agent analyzes failures, designs natural-language skill instructions, selects data, and retains skill context during fine-tuning. It costs an agentic pipeline for trajectory analysis, skill design, and iterative rollout-plus-evaluation feedback, plus the API or GPU expense of repeated teacher rollouts and target-model SFT, without reducing deployment cost. It can fail when the designed skills encode incorrect behavioral assumptions, when gains do not transfer beyond the evaluated terminal/search/SWE tasks, or when the reader's tasks lack verifiable evaluation signals to drive the autonomous feedback loop.
rationale: The method improves SFT data quality from an existing teacher without extra inference cost at deployment, but the autonomous skill-design agent pipeline is complex and its gains must be revalidated on the reader's own tasks before production reliance.

claims.statement: AutoMaster replaces Vanilla SFT on raw successful teacher trajectories with SFT on skill-guided trajectories, where an LLM agent analyzes failures, designs natural-language skill instructions, selects data, and retains skill context during fine-tuning. It costs an agentic pipeline for trajectory analysis, skill design, and iterative rollout-plus-evaluation feedback, plus the API or GPU expense of repeated teacher rollouts and target-model SFT, without reducing deployment cost. It can fail when the designed skills encode incorrect behavioral assumptions, when gains do not transfer beyond the evaluated terminal/search/SWE tasks, or when the reader's tasks lack verifiable evaluation signals to drive the autonomous feedback loop.

Improves mean performance over Vanilla SFT on unguided successful teacher trajectories by 1.42-8.99 percentage points across Terminal, Search, and SWE tasks with 4B and 9B targets, holding teacher, task pool, data size, and SFT recipe fixed.
